1

 Interest Of Justice.

This Petition, Coming On For Admission, This Day, The
 Court Made The Following:
 -2-
 Nc: 2023:Khc-K:1275
 Crl.P No. 200365 of 2023
 Order

The petitioner is sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 463,
464(A), 465, 468, 470, 471 of IPC, alleging that, the petitioner - accused when working as Deputy Director (Admin) prepared a seniority list of Teachers for promotion, and as per the direction of the Commissioner of Public Education Department, Bengaluru, conducted counseling on 28.4.2022 and 30.4.2022.
In the said counseling, though the candidates, remained absent, were promoted to the next cadre by concocting documents.
The registration of FIR is impugned in this petition.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1 - State.
3.

The order passed by the accused herein when he was working as Deputy Director promoting the candidates to the next higher cadre was withdrawn by the competent Authority, and the same was impugned by the candidates before the Karnataka Administrative Tribunal in Application Nos.20770 to 20795/2022.
The Administrative Tribunal, by order dated 6.1.2023, set aside the order canceling the order of promotion, however, liberty was reserved to take appropriate action in accordance with law.
4. The allegation is that, though the candidates had remained absent, they were promoted to the next higher post by concocting document.

The said allegation runs contrary to NC:
2023:KHC-K:1275 the fact that, the candidates, in fact, challenged the order revoking their promotion before the Karnataka Administrative Tribunal The promotion of the candidates was done in pursuance of the seniority list prepared by the Department of Promotional Committee.
The petitioner - accused as a Deputy Director is only required to conduct counseling of the candidates based on the seniority list sent by the Department of Promotional Committee.

5. The FIR was lodged, after the Karnataka Administrative Tribunal set aside the order canceling the promotion extended to the candidates, who had allegedly remained absent in the counseling conducted by the accused herein.

Whether the accused herein had promoted the candidates by concocting documents is the matter, which requires to be considered by the competent Authority in the light of the order passed by the Karnataka Administrative Tribunal.
Hence, the continuation of criminal proceeding will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER Narayan V Hosur vs State Of Karnataka on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149046467/
2 i) Criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned proceeding in Crime No.12/2023 pending on the file of the Principal Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) and CJM Court, Bijapur, District Bijapur, insofar as it relates to the petitioner -accused is hereby quashed.
